name: Blue Glacier (Standard Route)

waypoints.name: Hoh River Ranger Station
waypoints.directions: From US 101 about 13 miles south of Forks, turn east on Upper Hoh Road and drive about 18 miles to the road end at the Hoh Rain Forest Visitor Center, about 578 ft. A park entrance pass is required, and overnight trips need an Olympic National Park wilderness permit booked in advance; the Hoh is a quota area.

waypoints.name: Glacier Meadows
waypoints.directions: Follow the Hoh River Trail east up the valley past the Olympus Guard Station and Lewis Meadow, cross the High Hoh Bridge over the gorge, and climb past Elk Lake to Glacier Meadows at about 4,300 ft, roughly 17.5 miles. About a quarter mile below the meadows the trail crosses a washout on a ladder of roughly 100 ft with a fixed rope.

waypoints.name: Snow Dome
waypoints.directions: Take the climbers' way trail about 0.8 mile up onto the crest of the lateral moraine, follow the narrow, loose crest about 0.2 mile, then drop onto the toe of the Blue Glacier and rope up. Cross the glacier and climb roped to Snow Dome at about 6,600-6,800 ft.

waypoints.name: Mount Olympus (West Peak)
waypoints.directions: Stay roped and continue over Crystal Pass, scouting the large crevasse there for a usable snow bridge, then traverse south of and below Five Fingers Ridge toward the West Peak, which is hidden from the north. Cross the moat or bergschrund and climb the 80-ft summit tower by loose Class 4 ramps or the 5.4 north face.

approach: Start at the Hoh Ranger Station/Hoh Rain Forest trailhead (578 ft) inside Olympic National Park and follow the Hoh River Trail east. The first 10.5 miles to Lewis Meadows (1,005 ft) are gentle, shaded old-growth rainforest walking along the braided, glacially-fed Hoh River, with numerous log/stream crossings and abundant water the whole way. Continue past the Olympus Guard Station (~9 mi) and cross the High Hoh Bridge (a dramatic span hundreds of feet above the gorge, ~13.2 mi) into steeper, more exposed terrain. Reach Elk Lake (2,500 ft) around mile 15, where the trail begins climbing in earnest toward Glacier Meadows (4,200-4,300 ft, ~17.2-17.5 mi), the standard base camp. In early season expect several steep, consequential snow slopes between Elk Lake and Glacier Meadows requiring an ice axe and crampons. About 0.25 mile before Glacier Meadows the trail crosses a washout/slide area via a roughly 100 ft ladder (sometimes called the Jemrod Gully ladder) supplemented by a fixed rope; this is the crux of the hike-in for many parties. From Glacier Meadows, follow the climbers' way trail about 0.8 mile up onto the crest of the lateral moraine (a narrow, exposed 'catwalk' with loose rock underfoot), then along the moraine crest roughly 0.2 mile before descending onto the toe of the Blue Glacier itself (watch for rockfall on this descent). No camping is permitted between Glacier Meadows and the glacier. From Glacier Meadows the summit is roughly 4-6 more miles and about 3,700 ft of gain, roped up for crevasse travel from the glacier's edge, by way of Snow Dome (~6,600 ft) and the upper mountain; a notable hazard en route is a large crevasse near Crystal Pass that is often 'impassable' except via a snow bridge that must be scouted each season. Late June to mid-August is the best window for a straightforward glacier crossing.
